Reprehensible

rep-rih-HEN-suh-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Reprehensible is deserving strong blame or criticism; shamefully wrong.

The university expelled the graduate student after discovering that her prize-winning thesis contained three chapters lifted word-for-word from an unpublished colleague's work -- a plagiarism scandal every professor on the review board called reprehensible.

Worked Example

Historians widely agree that the company's reprehensible practice of ignoring worker safety complaints for a decade directly caused the factory disaster.

Reprehensible names conduct so wrong that it earns strong, often public condemnation -- it's a serious word, not used for minor mistakes.

How Reprehensible Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

blameworthy

blameworthy: deserving to be blamed

deplorable

deplorable: deserving strong disapproval

Antonyms

admirable

admirable: deserving respect and approval

commendable

commendable: worthy of praise

How Strong Is It? — unwise → unforgivable → reprehensible

unwise vs. reprehensible

unwise vs. reprehensible: Unwise just means a poor decision -- it doesn't necessarily deserve the strong moral condemnation that reprehensible carries.

unforgivable vs. reprehensible

unforgivable vs. reprehensible: Unforgivable goes even further than reprehensible, suggesting an act so wrong that it cannot even be pardoned.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — prehend-/hens-

root — prehend-/hens-: to seize, to grasp (Latin prehendere)

suffix — -ible

suffix — -ible: worthy of; able to be (Latin -ibilis)

Put it together

Put it together: Reprehensible comes from Latin re- ('back') + prehendere ('to seize, grasp') -- the same root behind apprehend, which police use when they 'seize' a suspect. Reprehensible conduct is, at root, conduct worth 'seizing back' on -- calling out and condemning.

Use the root in a new word: apprehend

Use the root in a new word: apprehend: Officers were able to apprehend the suspect just two blocks from the scene.

Word Choice

Reprehensible is a serious, formal word -- reserve it for conduct that genuinely deserves strong moral condemnation, not for small everyday slip-ups.
